objectives: Log in and open a program without step-by-step help.
Explain what we will make this term: a formatted document saved in two places.
Set my own TypingClub target for the term.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sign in, posture check, free practice while the class settles.

plan.title: Term reveal
plan.detail: Term theme: 'Typing & Documents'. Show the finished exemplar fact card they will make by Week 15. Explain the two-tool idea: Microsoft AND Google.

plan.title: Rules and routine recap
plan.detail: Recap the ICT room rules and the 5-step routine from Year 1. Quickfire: who can log in, open Word and close it in under 2 minutes?

plan.title: Diagnostic task
plan.detail: Type one sentence about the holidays, save it with own name. Note who needs support with typing, saving or the mouse - this sets the groupings for the term.

plan.title: My target
plan.detail: Each pupil writes their TypingClub target on the goal sheet (a star count or a level). Stick to the wall chart. Log out.

successCriteria: I logged in and opened a program on my own.
I typed and saved a sentence with my name on it.
I have written my typing target on the chart.

objectives: Keep my fingers on the home row while typing.
Choose accuracy before speed.
Reach the end of TypingClub Level 1 by half term.

plan.title: Hands ready
plan.detail: F and J bumps, elbows down, eyes on screen. 60-second warm-up drill on the home row only.

plan.title: Rhythm, not race
plan.detail: Model typing slowly with an even beat, then fast and messy. Ask which one scored better. Rule for the term: 'smooth beats fast'.

plan.title: TypingClub units
plan.detail: Independent unit work towards Level 1. Freeze for a posture check every 5 minutes. Support: cover hands with a card for children who peek.

plan.title: Accuracy stars
plan.detail: Each pupil records today's best accuracy on the wall chart. Celebrate anyone above 90% regardless of speed.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which letter is hardest to reach? Show it on the keyboard mat and practise ten times. Log out.

successCriteria: My fingers start and return to the home row.
My accuracy is 90% or better in at least one lesson.
I typed without looking down for a whole exercise.

objectives: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs.
Explain that two different tools can do the same job.
Type and save my name in each one.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Two tools, one job
plan.detail: Side-by-side on the big screen: Word and Docs. Spot the same buttons in both. Analogy: two shops that both sell bread.

plan.title: Word first
plan.detail: Open Word, type full name, make it big, save to OneDrive as name_word.docx. Model each step, pupils copy.

plan.title: Then Docs
plan.detail: Open Docs in the browser, type the same name. Notice: Docs saves by itself - there is no Save button. Rename the document to name_docs.

plan.title: Spot the difference
plan.detail: Class list: what was the same, what was different? Record on the comparison poster. Log out.

activities: Type and rename in Google Docs
successCriteria: I opened Word and Google Docs by myself.
I typed my name in both.
I can say one difference between them.

objectives: Type a paragraph of 3-4 sentences.
Use full stops and single spaces correctly.
Save the same paragraph in Word and in Docs.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What makes a sentence
plan.detail: Read the exemplar 'My Weekend' paragraph. Count the sentences, spot the capital letters and full stops.

plan.title: Plan out loud
plan.detail: Talk partners: say your three sentences before typing them. Prompt card: Who? Where? What did you do? How did you feel?

plan.title: Type it twice
plan.detail: Type the paragraph in Word, then copy the same into Docs. Rule: one space after a full stop, capital letter at the start of each sentence.

plan.title: Partner proofread
plan.detail: Swap seats and check a partner's paragraph for capitals and full stops. Fix and re-save. Log out.

activities: 'My Weekend' paragraph in Word and Docs
successCriteria: My paragraph has 3 or more sentences.
Every sentence starts with a capital and ends with a full stop.
The paragraph is saved in both Word and Docs.

objectives: Highlight text with the mouse or Shift + arrows.
Apply Bold, Italic and Underline.
Explain why we make some words stand out.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why format?
plan.detail: Show the same paragraph plain and formatted. Which is easier to read? Rule: formatting helps the reader, it is not decoration.

plan.title: Highlight first
plan.detail: The hard part is selecting text. Practise three ways: click-drag, double-click a word, Shift + arrow keys. Everyone selects the same three words.

plan.title: B, I, U
plan.detail: Open last week's paragraph. Make two important words Bold, the title Italic, one keyword Underlined. Same again in the Docs copy.

plan.title: Gallery check
plan.detail: Show three screens on the projector. Ask: is the formatting helping or shouting? Save and log out.

activities: Bold / Italic / Underline on own paragraph
successCriteria: I can select exactly the words I want.
I used bold, italic and underline for a reason.
My changes are saved in both files.

objectives: Change the font, size and colour of text.
Choose colours that are easy to read.
Say why yellow text on white is a bad choice.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Readable or not?
plan.detail: Show five colour combinations on the board. Vote readable / not readable. Introduce the word contrast.

plan.title: Font, size, colour
plan.detail: Demo the three dropdowns. Make the title 24pt in a dark colour, the body 12pt in black. Pupils copy on their paragraph.

plan.title: Design challenge
plan.detail: Make the paragraph look good with a maximum of two fonts and two colours. Constraint teaches restraint.

plan.title: Swap and rate
plan.detail: Partner rates readability out of 3. One improvement suggested and applied. Save, log out.

successCriteria: I changed the font, size and colour of my text.
My text is easy to read from a metre away.
I used no more than two fonts.

objectives: Insert a picture from a folder into my document.
Resize a picture using the corner handles.
Move a picture to where I want it.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Corner handles rule
plan.detail: Demo stretching a photo from the side (squashed face) versus the corner (still correct). Rule: always drag the corner.

plan.title: Insert a picture
plan.detail: Insert > Picture > from the class picture folder. Pupils choose one image and insert it into their paragraph document.

plan.title: Resize and place
plan.detail: Resize with corner handles to about a third of the page, then drag it beside the text. Repeat in the Docs copy.

plan.title: Squash spotting
plan.detail: Project two examples: one squashed, one correct. Class spots the difference. Save and log out.

activities: Insert image from the class folder
successCriteria: I inserted a picture into my document.
My picture is the right shape, not squashed.
My picture sits where I wanted it.

objectives: Save one file to Google Drive and one to Microsoft OneDrive.
Use the class file-naming rule: Firstname_Topic.
Find my own file again after saving.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Two clouds
plan.detail: Explain: Drive belongs to Google, OneDrive belongs to Microsoft. Both keep the file safe even if the computer breaks.

plan.title: Naming rule
plan.detail: Bad names on the board: doc1, asdf, Untitled. Good names: Aisha_Weekend. Everyone renames their two files to the rule.

plan.title: Save to both
plan.detail: Save the Word file to OneDrive, and check the Docs file is in Drive. Then close everything and find both again - this proves it worked.

plan.title: Find-it race
plan.detail: Timed: open both files from the cloud. Log out.

successCriteria: My file names follow Firstname_Topic.
One copy is in Drive and one is in OneDrive.
I can find my files again after closing them.

objectives: Choose an animal and find three facts about it.
Type the facts into a fact card layout.
Work in both Word and Docs without help.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Exemplar study
plan.detail: Look at the finished fact card exemplar. Identify the parts: title, 3 facts, picture, caption.

plan.title: Choose and gather
plan.detail: Choose an animal from the class list. Use the printed fact sheet (not open web search) to pick three facts.

plan.title: Draft the text
plan.detail: Type the title and three fact sentences into the template. Formatting comes next week - today is words only.

plan.title: Read back
plan.detail: Read your card to a partner. Does each fact make sense on its own? Save and log out.

activities: Choose an animal and pick 3 facts
successCriteria: I chose an animal and found three facts.
My card has a title and three fact sentences.
My draft is saved in Word and Docs.

objectives: Apply formatting and a picture to my fact card.
Save the finished card to both clouds.
Check my work against the marking rubric.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Read the rubric
plan.detail: Share the exam rubric in pupil language: typed paragraph, 3 formatting changes, one picture, saved twice. Tick list on the wall.

plan.title: Format and illustrate
plan.detail: Apply bold, a title colour and a font change; insert and resize the animal picture. Follow the corner-handles rule.

plan.title: Save to both clouds
plan.detail: Drive and OneDrive, correct file name. Partner checks both saves happened.

plan.title: Rubric self-check
plan.detail: Tick your own rubric. Anything unticked is your job next lesson. Log out.

activities: Format and illustrate the fact card
successCriteria: My card has at least three formatting changes.
My card has a picture that is the right shape.
My card is saved in both Drive and OneDrive.

objectives: Type a short paragraph on my own.
Apply three formatting changes.
Insert a picture and save the file once as a Google file and once as a Microsoft file.

plan.title: Settle and brief
plan.detail: Read the task card aloud twice. Rubric visible on the board. Remind: work alone, hand up for technical help only.

plan.title: Type the paragraph
plan.detail: Given prompt, 3-4 sentences. Circulate silently, note who needs the routine card.

plan.title: Format and picture
plan.detail: Three formatting changes plus one inserted, correctly sized picture from the class folder.

plan.title: Save twice
plan.detail: Save to OneDrive and to Drive with the correct file name. This step carries the most marks - remind at 5 minutes remaining.

plan.title: Close down
plan.detail: Everyone closes files and logs out properly. Collect task cards.

successCriteria: I typed a paragraph without help.
I made three formatting changes.
I inserted a picture correctly.
I saved the file as both a Google and a Microsoft file.

objectives: Add a second paragraph to my fact card.
Write a caption underneath my picture.
Check a partner's spelling and fix my own.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a caption?
plan.detail: Look at captions in a real non-fiction book. A caption tells you what the picture shows in one short line.

plan.title: Second paragraph
plan.detail: Add three more sentences: where the animal lives, what it eats, one surprising fact.

plan.title: Add the caption
plan.detail: Type a one-line caption under the picture in a smaller font size.

plan.title: Peer spell-check
plan.detail: Swap with a partner using the peer-check sheet. Fix at least one thing. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My card now has two paragraphs.
My picture has a caption under it.
I fixed at least one spelling my partner found.

objectives: Pick a colour from my picture and use it for my title.
Explain why matching colours looks joined-up.
Apply the idea to my whole card.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Colour matching demo
plan.detail: Project a photo of a tiger. Pick the orange from the fur for the title colour. Show before and after - the class always sees the difference immediately.

plan.title: Apply it
plan.detail: Use the font colour dropdown (or eyedropper in Docs) to choose a colour taken from their own picture and apply it to the title.

plan.title: One more touch
plan.detail: Optional: match the caption colour too, but keep body text black for readability.

plan.title: Before and after
plan.detail: Show two or three cards before and after on the projector. Save and log out.

activities: Apply a picture colour to the title
successCriteria: My title colour comes from my picture.
My body text is still easy to read.
I can explain why the card looks joined-up.

objectives: Export or print my fact card.
Present it to a partner in two full sentences.
Add my card to the class portfolio wall.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Print or PDF
plan.detail: Demo File > Print, and File > Download as PDF. Explain when each is useful. Manage the printer queue by table.

plan.title: Presentation practice
plan.detail: Sentence stems: 'My animal is ___. The most interesting fact is ___.' Practise twice with a partner.

plan.title: Portfolio wall
plan.detail: Pin the printed card to the wall display. Everyone reads three cards from the wall.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which card taught you something new? Name it and say why. Log out.

successCriteria: My card is printed or exported as a PDF.
I presented my card in two full sentences.
My card is on the portfolio wall.

objectives: Read three classmates' fact cards carefully.
Write two stars and a wish for someone else's work.
Say one thing I improved this term.

plan.title: How to give feedback
plan.detail: Model a kind wish versus an unkind one. Rule: talk about the work, never the person.

plan.title: Gallery walk
plan.detail: Walk the portfolio wall with sticky notes. Read three cards, leave two stars and one wish on each.

plan.title: Read my feedback
plan.detail: Return to your own card and read the notes left for you. Circle the wish you would act on first.

plan.title: Term reflection
plan.detail: Complete the sentence: 'In ICT this term I got better at ___.' Add it to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Class round of applause; name three skills learned since August. Log out.

successCriteria: I gave two stars and a wish on three cards.
My feedback is kind and about the work.
I named one thing I got better at this term.
